chief_complaint: right shoulder pain on overhead painting, Neer positive
hpi_details: A 29-year-old male presents to the clinic with right shoulder pain on overhead painting, neer positive. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks he popped his shoulder slightly out of alignment or tore a muscle while straining to paint a high ceiling.
concerns: He is worried that his shoulder will freeze up and require surgery, which would cause him to lose his independent painting contracts.
expectations: He hopes to get an X-ray to confirm nothing is torn and receive a cortisone injection so he can finish his current painting job this week.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Rotator Cuff Impingement evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Rotator Cuff Impingement is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Rotator Cuff Impingement: Physical therapy (rotator cuff/scapular), subacromial injection, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Rotator Cuff Impingement.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Soft tissue strain without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Severe progressive motor deficit.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of right shoulder pain on overhead painting, Neer positive. HPI: rotator cuff impingement.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Rotator Cuff Impingement.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Rotator Cuff Impingement.
reference_soap.plan: For suspected rotator cuff impingement, use physical therapy focused on rotator-cuff and scapular rehabilitation. Consider a clinician-performed subacromial corticosteroid injection only after diagnostic reassessment and an inadequate response to conservative care; arrange specialist review for persistent symptoms or progressive weakness. Counsel the patient.

must_ask.say: Did the shoulder pain start after a lot of overhead reaching or activity, like painting?
Is the pain worst in a specific range when you lift your arm, like between shoulder and ear height?

must_ask.objective: Night pain when lying on shoulder
must_ask.say: Does the pain wake you up at night, especially when lying on that shoulder?
Do you feel true weakness lifting your arm, or is it mainly pain stopping you?
Have you tried any physical therapy, rest, or injections, and what activities are you hoping to get back to?

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, temperature 36.6°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Well-developed, alert young male in no acute distress, holding his right arm guarded slightly close to his torso.

No erythema, swelling, or deformity of either shoulder; focal tenderness over the right anterior acromion and greater tuberosity; active abduction triggers pain between 60 and 120 degrees with a positive Neer impingement sign on the right; passive range of motion is preserved.
Normal 5/5 motor strength in bilateral upper extremities, with pain-limited effort during right shoulder abduction and external rotation; no muscle atrophy or true motor deficit.
Intact light touch and pinprick sensation bilaterally across C5 through T1 dermatomes, including over the right lateral deltoid area.
Biceps, triceps, and brachioradialis deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric bilaterally.
Cervical spine has full active range of motion without midline tenderness or radiating symptoms on Spurling testing.
No rashes, psoriatic plaques, tophi, or nail abnormalities noted.
